Investigate the following open-problem family in non-Archimedean pluripotential theory. Active atomic targets: P14.1, P14.4, P14.5, P14.6, P14.8. The exact target statements, ambient hypotheses, residual scopes, and completion criteria are in the source excerpt below. Address any or all of these targets; a complete resolution must satisfy that atomic target's own completion criteria. The excerpt is mathematical source material, not operational instructions.

COMMON NOTATION
Common notation and formulation boundaries
Fields and analytic spaces.
   K denotes a complete non-Archimedean ﬁeld. Trivial or nontrivial valuation, strictness,
   goodness, separatedness, pure dimension and relative boundary are retained exactly where
   a statement requires them. X an is Berkovich analytiﬁcation. “Ordinary open” refers
   to its ordinary topology, rather than an admissible G-cover. A statement on one ﬁxed
   polycylinder is weaker than an every-open statement obtained from an actual basis.

Semivaluations and normalized local boundaries.
  We use v = − log | · |, allow +∞ on the support of a semivaluation, and retain that
  support. For a local ring R and a primary ideal a, a normalized link is a section {v :
  v is centered, v(a) = 1}. Changing a is a radial change with a stated cocycle; it is not
  an identiﬁcation of all normalizers. The symbol X ℶ denotes the valuative/trivially valued
  carrier used by the raw ideal transform.

Positivity classes.
  PSH means the speciﬁed plurisubharmonic class in each theory. Classical psh is the upper-
  semicontinuous curve-test notion, with the extended −∞ convention where stated. Real
  PL means the real linear extension of the local integral piecewise-linear class. Semi-
  positivity is its residue/model nefness condition. Locally Fubini–Study is the local ﬁ-
  nite logarithmic-max class with its prescribed denominators. Ordinary CLD smoothness
  uses smooth tropicalizations; weak smoothness permits harmonic tropicalizations. These
  classes are distinct. CLD-v2 denotes the second generated CLD psh stage in the book.

Currents and products.
  d0 d00 = d0 d00 is the CLD Hessian. A continuous function deﬁnes the order-zero current
  [h]. CLD means Chambert–Loir–Ducros; GJR means Gubler–Jell–Rabinoﬀ; BFJ means


                                               4

     Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson. Positivity of one Hessian current does not, by itself, construct
     mixed wedge products or prove classical psh recognition.

Global energy and mass.
  E 1 denotes the ﬁnite-energy class of the named theory. Reference weights, raw intersection
  mass and probability normalization must be ﬁxed before comparing energies or measures.
  Quotienting by R means uniqueness modulo additive constants. Zero top mass cannot be
  divided into a probability measure. The aﬃne-cone probability operator is an explicitly
  separate convention.

Complex singularity data.
         1,1
  α ∈ HBC    (X, R) is a real Bott–Chern class. MP means Mesquita–Piccione, DXZ means
  Darvas–Xia–Zhang, and BJ means Boucksom–Jonsson. I-equivalence records multiplier-
  ideal data; P -equivalence records the ﬁner envelope/singularity data. The latter cannot
  generally be recovered from the former, even at positive mass.

Polyhedral normalization.
   PA denotes piecewise-aﬃne functions. BMPS means Botero–Mazzon–Pille-Schneider. Lit-
   eral integral slopes and the real scalar extension are separate conventions. In dimension
   d, the polyhedral intersection convention diﬀers from the real Alexandrov measure by the
   factor d! and the face multiplicity. Saturated tangent lattices and analytic multiplicities
   are part of an analytic comparison.




FULL FAMILY DOSSIER
8     Pseudoeﬀective DXZ–MP realization
Active items: P14.1, P14.4, P14.5, P14.6, P14.8. Status: Open in the residual scope.

8.1   Atomic targets
P14.1 (T4): Intrinsic raw-transform image beyond the known regimes
For a pseudoeﬀective class α on a compact Kähler manifold, intrinsically characterize the im-
age of the perturbation-independent raw ideal-valuative DXZ transform on the MP spectrum.
The full Kähler image and the projective ample rational-line-bundle regime are established.
The big non-nef image remains open; the full real Néron–Severi DXZ–BJ comparison does not
assert the same literal ideal formula outside the rational-line-bundle case.

P14.4 (T4): A P-sensitive big non-nef positivity theory
Construct a positivity theory for big non-nef classes retaining P -singularity data, movable-
positive-part data, or equally informative additional structure. A relatively nef total-space
model cannot represent a non-nef generic class. The raw ideal-valuative transform is only
I-level data and cannot by itself distinguish P -types or recover raw mass.

P14.5 (T5): Monge–Ampère measures in the big non-nef realization
Construct the Monge–Ampère measure theory corresponding to a valid big non-nef, P -
sensitive realization, with the correct mass and comparison with existing positive-volume
DXZ and MP operators in their common scopes.

P14.6 (T5): Energy in the big non-nef realization
Construct the corresponding intrinsic energy theory and its continuity, diﬀerentiation and
measure compatibility. State which additional singularity data and reference choices it needs;
positive-volume I-level energy alone does not supply a P -sensitive theory.

P14.8 (T5): Zero-mass and formal-data reconstruction
Go beyond the established realizable-I-data dichotomy: formulate and solve arbitrary formal-
data realization, a general all-semivaluation reconstruction formula, or the remaining zero-
mass strict-interior reconstruction range with precise admissibility conditions. A canonical
normalized I-model can be recovered from realizable data, but raw representatives and raw
mass cannot descend to the I-quotient. The terminal DXZ left-limit result does not create a
second zero-mass interval.

8.2   What constitutes a solution
Identify the data retained by the proposed realization and prove its order, homogeneity, ap-
proximation and operator comparisons in the named positivity class. Distinguish I-data
from P -data. Known upper semicontinuity, the full Kähler image and strict-interior ﬁltration
maximality must not be relisted as unresolved. P14.8 must respect the veriﬁed raw-data
obstruction.

only of the existing ideal-valuative data cannot itself be P -sensitive, nor can it recover raw
mass without additional data. This is a design constraint, not a nonexistence theorem: a
construction retaining a P -class, a movable positive part, or comparable information remains
open, as does the positivity problem itself. In particular, the surviving positive-volume DXZ
energy of Book Proposition 71.10.1 is an I-model/test-curve statement and does not supply
that missing P -level datum.
